The EPOS H3 Hybrid is on sale for just $24.99 at Woot , a whopping 75 percent off its original price of $99.99. It has an unorthodox batch of features: USB-A and 3.5mm options for connecting to a controller or a PC, and Bluetooth support for listening to music and taking calls. Notably, it can play audio from wired and wireless sources concurrently, and it can last up to 37 hours per charge. EPOS H3 Hybrid Where to Buy: $99.99 $24.99 at Woot My colleague Cameron Faulkner spent some time with the wired-only version of this headset five years ago, and was impressed by its balanced sound profile, comfortable fit, and generously-sized volume knob. He had some qualms about USB connectivity and lack of sidetone, both of which seem to have been addressed in the Hybrid version of the headset that’s available at a steep discount right now. This version also has two microphones — a removable boom mic and a built-in microphone — so you can still take calls via Bluetooth without looking like an airline pilot. ]]> Sean Hollister https://www.theverge.com/?p=971963 2026-07-28T15:12:48-04:00 2026-07-28T15:12:48-04:00 In June, Nintendo announced a new version of the Switch 2 that should let you easily replace its battery pack - but only for Europe. For families that contain both Android and Apple devices, it might be better to pick up the latest Tile Pro instead. It works well across both platforms, and right now it’s on sale for $23.99 ($11 off) at Amazon and directly from Tile . This is its cheapest price in 2026 so far and only $1 shy of the all-time low we saw in October. Tile Pro Where to Buy: $34.99 $23.99 at Amazon $34.99 $23.99 at Tile As Tile’s most capable tracker, the Pro offers a Bluetooth range of up to 500 feet and the loudest ring of its lineup at 110 decibels, making it easier to locate misplaced items nearby. While it doesn’t tap into Apple’s Find My or Google’s Find Hub networks, its Life360 app remains a reliable option for keeping tabs on valuables both near and far.  The Tile Pro can also save you a little money in a few ways compared to Apple’s AirTag.  For starters, it includes a built-in keyring hole, so you can attach it to your keys, backpack, or luggage without buying a separate holder.
